key_insight: Localized carrier spins in metal-halide perovskites relax mainly through hyperfine coupling to nuclear spins, with holes dominated by metal nuclei and electrons by halogen nuclei.
engineering_relevance: Understanding and controlling hyperfine-driven spin relaxation can help tune carrier spin lifetimes, localization, and readout strategies in perovskite optoelectronic and spintronic devices.
method: Adapted an exact spin-relaxation model originally developed for muon spin spectroscopy.
Handled arbitrary hyperfine correlation times, including the intermediate regime where mono-exponential fits break down.
Applied the model to time-resolved Faraday rotation data from two perovskite samples to extract microscopic parameters.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that fits to time-resolved Faraday rotation data from two samples recover carrier localization volume and hyperfine correlation time, showing the exact solution outperforms a single-exponential approximation.
watch_item: The model is focused on localized carriers and hyperfine relaxation, so results may not directly transfer to delocalized carriers or samples where additional spin-relaxation mechanisms dominate.
paper_title: Hyperfine driven spin relaxation of charge carriers in metal-halide perovskites
